transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time on short notice. As you know, we've received a credible report that our authorized distributor routed some medical-device orders through an unfamiliar sub-distributor in a restricted market. No actions have been taken yet — no shipment suspension, no regulatory disclosure, no contractual notice, no termination decision. Before I approve the written response package, I need a clear status round from each of you. Let's start with sanctions: what's your preliminary read on the restricted-market implications? Then contracts on our rights and obligations, and finally client-operations on hospital-system exposure.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share critical findings before we go any further. I completed transaction screening this morning and confirmed that two shipments went to an Iran-linked reseller not covered by any applicable OFAC general license. My report requires immediate suspension of distributor shipments and a voluntary OFAC disclosure filed within exactly 10 days. I have not circulated the report yet, but given where we are in this discussion, everyone needs to know this now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to add critical contract information before we proceed. I retrieved and reviewed the executed distribution agreement from the contract archive this morning. Its compliance-breach clause requires a written cure notice giving exactly 10 business days, identifying the offending shipments, before termination can take effect. This clause is absent from the current incident summary, so we need to account for it in any response package.
